blogs.title: Spotting Mody When the Age Cut‐off Isn’t Enough
blogs.description:
Emerging evidence shows many patients diagnosed before 25 actually fall outside conventional screening rules because family history alone can drive suspicion.

This post explains how clinicians should broaden their index of suspicion when patients display nonautoimmune hyperglycaemia—even if their BMI looks normal or even elevated—and how even patients slightly older than the classic ‘early‑onset’ window can harbor MODY.

Using the Exeter probability calculator as an example—highlighting its strengths and limitations in Asian populations—we explore practical ways teams can flag candidates for genetic testing before defaulting to type I or type II labels.

blogs.title: From Basal Insulin To GLP‑RAs — Tailoring Therapy in HNF1A‐MODY
blogs.description:
Despite initial treatment often mirroring type II regimens (basal insulin + metformin), patients with an HNF1A mutation typically benefit far more from agents that potentiate β‑cell function.

We dissect why sulfonylureas were first thought ideal, review recent trials comparing glimepiride versus liraglutide, explain the practical decision tree once genetics confirms MODY—moving swiftly from insulin shaders toward lower‐hypoglycaemia GLP‑RA options—and discuss expected outcomes such evolving HbAµ1 ––12% suppression seen within months.”},{

blogs.title: Missing Medicine — Why SGLT‑2 Inhibitors Are Doomed In HNF1A‐MODY
blogs.description:
Patients harbouring mutations affecting hepatic nuclear factor Iα often exhibit an intrinsic downregulation of renal GLUT‐SGLT transporters.

This post reviews mechanistic data showing fol upwards renal threshold deficits paired with stretched susceptibility for volume depletion, genital candida superinfection and euglycaemic ketoacidosis.

We’ll outline real‑world reports where sglt‑2 drugs precipitated DKA crises once hypoglycaemic backing lost its protective effect—and give you a short decision mnemonic you can carry into your next infusion round.”

blogs.title: Detecting Ominiatized Autonomic Dysfunction Early With Sudoscan
blogs.description:
In this rare form of MODY neuroevaluation isn’t always part of standard practice – yet subtle sudomotor changes can appear months before overt retinopathy.

This post covers use cases citing our patient’s severely diminished electrochemical skin conductance detecting small fibre loss despite normal microalbuminuria.

Clinicians learn why incorporating Sudoscan—or similar reflexive autonomic batteries—is critical in young diabetics when judging progression risk beyond HbAµ18 cardiometabolic surrogates.
